summary: The reported prefill defect was reproduced by reconstructing the pre-fix constexpr signature from the checked-out implementation. Four representative expanded-page-table row strides produced four Triton cache keys and four distinct HSACO binaries. Main already contains upstream PR #37093: page_table_stride_0 is a runtime do_not_specialize argument, and the same strides reuse one cache key and one HSACO while matching an independent PyTorch reference exactly. No duplicate source fix was applied.

tests.what_was_measured: Nine GPU tests covering exact numerical correctness, dynamic prefill strides, specialization count, padding, empty batches, batch size 8192, context lengths through 1,000,000, decode output, and zero decode row stride.

Actual Triton in-memory cache keys and SHA-256 identities of generated gfx950 HSACO for row strides 4096, 4160, 4224, and 65537, plus exact comparison with an independent torch.gather reference. Pre-fix counts were 1/2/3/4 with four distinct binaries; current counts were 1/1/1/1 with one binary.

remaining_limitations: The CUDA-specific cuModuleLoadData lock and long-lived NVIDIA process memory growth were not directly measured on this ROCm-only assigned GPU. The compiler-level cause and bounded identity behavior were measured with Triton 3.7.0 on gfx950. Decode was intentionally not changed: its operational page table comes from fixed-width preallocated request/CUDA-graph storage, unlike the contiguous expanded prefill table whose row stride follows each context length. No FlyDSL C++ code changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
